name: Slagside Rivet-Chain Utility Belt
description:
Heavy-gauge recycled conveyor-belt rubber stitched with salvaged copper rivets and mismatched industrial clasps. The surface is oil-stained matte black with patches of oxidized orange where the original factory stamping shows through. Loop spacing is irregular — clearly assembled by hand rather than machine — but the D-rings and snap hooks are rated for actual load-bearing use.

Multiple hanging points accommodate tools, pouches, and jury-rigged holsters. A secondary strap threads through the main belt for stability under weight. Shelf staple.
functionality: Six load-bearing D-rings, four snap hooks, two wide tool loops, and a hidden inner pocket sealed with a rusted zipper. Distributes up to 15kg of gear without slipping. Compatible with leg-strap holster attachments.
what_it_says: This person builds what they need from what's left over, and they've been doing it long enough to do it well.
story_hooks: One of the D-rings is stamped with a Crucible Industries lot number from a factory that burned down six years ago — someone knows what that means.
A courier was found dead with this belt still buckled, every pouch empty except for a single encrypted data chip wedged under the inner pocket zipper.
A Tier 3 fashion blogger posted a photo wearing one ironically; Shelf residents are not amused.
